"fab40d01-6a17-5e12-835f-851b2c004a35" :question/problem "Express the following as a constant multiple of a single trigonometric ratio.

$$
6\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{9}\right)\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{9}\right)
$$"] [:db/add "fab40d01-6a17-5e12-835f-851b2c004a35" :question/worked-solution "Put $x=\frac{2\pi}{9}$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

\begin{aligned}
6\sin x\cos x &=3\left[2\sin x\cos x\right] \\ &=3\sin(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

$$

knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=\frac{\pi}{7}$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{-\sin x\cos x}{2\cos(2x)} &=-\frac{1}{4}\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=-\frac{1}{4}\frac{\sin(2x)}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=-\frac{1}{4}\tan(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

The denominator is nonzero, and $\tan(2x)=\sin(2x)/\cos(2x)$.

Substitute $x=\frac{\pi}{7}$ and double the whole angle: $2x=\frac{2\pi}{7}$. The result is

$$
-\frac{1}{4}\tan\left(\frac{2\pi}{7}\right) .
$$

knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=17^\circ$. Expand the square and combine the squared terms.

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\sin x+\cos x)^2 &=\sin^2 x+2\sin x\cos x+\cos^2 x \\ &=1+2\sin x\cos x \\ &=1+\sin(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x=1$ and $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$. Multiply both terms by $3$.

Substitute $x=17^\circ$ and double the whole angle: $2x=34^\circ$. The result is

$$
3+3\sin\left(34^\circ\right) .
$$
